case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports [1987] 1 Sri L.R. 293

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was produced before a Magistrate within the time required by law and thus whether his detention violated Article 13(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner was produced before the Magistrate three days later than the 30 days allowed by the proviso to Regulation 19(1), violating Article 13(2).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents argued the detention was authorized under Emergency Regulations and that the delay was minor.
key_facts: Petitioner arrested on 22 May 1985 and produced before Magistrate on 25 June 1985.
Regulation 19(1) requires production before Magistrate within 30 days of arrest.
Petitioner was produced three days late, violating the proviso to Regulation 19(1).
Article 13(2) requires detainees to be brought before a judge according to law.
Court held Article 13(2) must be read with proviso to Regulation 19(1).

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 13(2) safeguards personal liberty by requiring detainees to be produced before a judge within a reasonable time, here interpreted in conjunction with Emergency Regulation 19(1) proviso as 30 days.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The petitioner was produced three days after the 30-day limit, constituting a violation of Article 13(2).
principles_established: Article 13(2) must be strictly complied with by the executive.
Emergency Regulations proviso to Regulation 19(1) is incorporated into Article 13(2) for procedural safeguards.
Delay in production before Magistrate, even if short, violates constitutional rights.
precedents_cited: Yasapalitha Nanayakkara v. Henry Perera and Others S.C. Application No. 19/85

outcome.holding: The belated production of the petitioner before the Magistrate was a violation of Article 13(2).
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The petitioner was awarded Rs. 5,000 compensation payable by the State and costs of the application.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: The court’s central holding was that the delay in producing the petitioner before a Magistrate violated Article 13(2), which protects personal liberty by requiring timely judicial oversight.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner was produced before the Magistrate three days after the 30-day period allowed by Regulation 19(1), which the court held violated Article 13(2).
